neighbours.label: finite 'be' (is/was/were/will be) after a noun-phrase subject, typically a passive or predicative clause
fire: Under the new treaty, free passage was guaranteed to all merchant ships.
Many critics argued that the proposed tax would be a burden on small farmers.
Great care is taken to preserve the original wooden beams.
Although strong objections were raised, the council approved the plan.
The ancient city is still remarkably well preserved.
Little attention has been paid to the role of women in the strike.
In the old village, water was carried up from the river every morning.
Their fear is that the bridge will be closed for another year.
quiet: Under the new treaty, merchant ships gained free passage through the strait.
Many critics argued that the proposed tax would burden small farmers.
The builders took great care to preserve the original wooden beams.
Although residents raised strong objections, the council approved the plan.
Visitors still admire the remarkably preserved ancient city.
Historians have paid little attention to the role of women in the strike.
In the old village, women carried water up from the river every morning.
They fear that officials will close the bridge for another year.

notes: Card: top 32 peaks are ' was' x9, ' is' x7, ' be' x5, ' been', ' were', mostly after an abstract-noun subject (hopes were held, thought is bestowed, travel was to be assured). The + pole also peaks on be-forms (modal 'needs to be looked at'), so the split may be finite-after-subject vs after-modal.
